title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: M_G ≅ M_{G'} under découpage holds only for strata rigidified by the graph (labelled half-edges). On the usual unrigidified boundary strata the gluing map is a quotient by Aut(G), not an isomorphism.

Variance in 2) is unclear: for a forgetful map M_{g,ν} -> M_{g,ν'} with ν' ⊂ ν, the injection goes from the smaller leg set to the larger. That fits the induction-type morphism G' -> G inducing M_G -> M_{G'}, rather than an ordinary hom G -> G' inducing M_G -> M_{G'}. Grothendieck seems aware of this, adding the 'immersion' condition and then introducing induction homs.

'Ne passent pas aux compactifiés' is true only for naive extension to M̂_G -> M̂_{G'}. Knudsen's stabilisation does give M̄_{g,n+1} -> M̄_{g,n}, but it does not respect the stratum closures M̂_G type-wise, because contraction of unstable components changes the graph.

missed.claim: An early (c. 1978–81) systematic attempt to define a category of decorated dual graphs whose morphism types (contraction, cutting/gluing, and 'induction' maps that are origin-compatible and injective on stars but not σ-compatible) act functorially on the strata M_G, M̂_G and universal curves. This anticipates the graph categories behind modular operads (Getzler–Kapranov) and especially Borisov–Manin and Joyal–Kock style morphisms.
missed.quote: Hom. d'induction de MD-graphes ... compatibilité avec application origine ... (mais pas compatible avec application extrémité, ni avec σ, σ') ... u_1 : Â'_{s'} → Â_s injectif
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical. It documents that Grothendieck's Teichmüller-tower programme rested on an explicit graph-category formalism, predating the operadic literature. The 'induction' morphisms (star-injective, leg-to-edge) resemble the étale/embedding maps in Joyal–Kock graphical categories.

deep.surprise_reason: Content is mostly standard clutching and forgetful-map formalism. The careful definition of induction morphisms of graphs is an early version of graph categories later developed independently. This is interesting historically but not a new result.
